question: An element 'A' reacts with chlorine to give a compound ACl with a high melting point. This compound is also soluble in water. The element 'A' is likely to be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sodium**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sodium** reacts with chlorine to form sodium chloride (NaCl),** which has a high melting point and is soluble in water.
 
• This reaction releases a large amount of heat and forms a stable ionic compound.
 
• **Sodium chloride (NaCl) is highly soluble in water, which aligns with the compound described in the question.**
 
• Sodium chloride has a relatively high melting point (~801°C), which matches the description of the compound having a high melting point.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The melting point of a substance is the t**emperature at which it changes from a solid to a liquid.**
 
• At this temperature, the solid and liquid phases of the substance exist in equilibrium
 
• The melting point of a substance depends on pressure and is usually specified at a standard pressure.
 
• During **the melting process, the substance absorbs heat and the temperature remains constant.** 
 
• The melting point of a pure substance is a single temperature, but the melting point of a solution of two or more components is usually a range of temperatures. 
 
• The melting point of a **substance is a characteristic property of solid crystalline substances. **
 
• **The melting point of a substance is used to evaluate structural changes in organic compoun**ds.
